zeroclaw-api.reason: Composition ports, model/tool/channel/memory traits, principal identity and observer events; this is the capability contract owner.

zeroclaw-config.reason: Authoritative schema3 config generation, policy resolution and admitted agent identity; the runtime keeps enforcement and resolves live state at use time.

zeroclaw-spawn.reason: Existing process/sandbox execution ownership for the compatibility shell tool and managed background children.

zeroclaw-infra.reason: Existing ACP session persistence and key-free filesystem/HTTP support; the session lifecycle owns those handles.

zeroclaw-tls.reason: Existing runtime network clients use the shared TLS provider; no adapter selection authority is supplied by this edge.

zeroclaw-relay-proto.reason: Existing daemon relay bridge imports control/data framing, connection-window and rate-limit types at crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/relay.rs:34. The relay bridge and its connection/cancellation lifecycle remain runtime-owned.

zeroclaw-commands.reason: Existing RPC command catalogue imports CommandSurface and commands_for_surface at crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs:34 and projects the TUI catalogue into InitializeResult at :3707. This catalogue owner is distinct from provider/memory/tool selection.

zeroclaw-log.reason: Canonical attributed runtime events and observer projection; the turn lifecycle is the producer.

zeroclaw-providers.reason: Compatibility ConfigProviders, existing provider-switch adapter and doctor/quickstart probes still construct native providers; generic capability entries must never invoke them. Agent model-route resolution also uses the shared router value without constructing a concrete provider. Application composition owns default-source selection.

zeroclaw-memory.reason: Compatibility ConfigMemory and legacy memory-free ACP adapters still open or substitute native memory; existing response/session caches retain their memory owner. Generic supplied-memory requests must use MemorySource. Application composition owns default backend selection.

zeroclaw-tools.reason: The compatibility native registry owns host-coupled tool handles and the existing tier1/tier2 tools; ScopedToolRegistry owns policy/MCP/skill filtering. Generic supplied-tool requests must not invoke the native factory. Application composition owns default adapter selection; retention cannot justify constructing native tools on the consumer path.

zeroclaw-sop-graph.reason: Existing SOP graph/state definitions owned by the SOP engine; no additional composition capability.

zeroclaw-plugins.reason: Existing optional runtime plugin adapter boundary and host lifetime; policy and reservations remain enforced by the registry. Optionality does not excuse concrete construction on a supplied-capability path.

zeroclaw-tool-call-parser.reason: Canonical native/text tool-call parser used by the real engine.

zeroclaw-macros.reason: Existing compile-time attribution/registration helpers used by runtime-owned agent and tools; no concrete adapter selection or runtime policy cache.
